description.narrative:
Program för att stötta Mocambiques nationella arbetsmarknadspolitik och skapa fler och bättre jobb på sektornivå. Det övergripand emålet är att bidra till produktiv sysselsättning med anständiga arbetsvillkor för mocambikiska kvinnor och män, i synnerhet unga människor och människor i fattigdom. Tre underliggande resultatmål förväntas bidra till det övergripande målet: - Resultat 1 (nationellt): Understödjande ekonomisk och sektoriell politik och arbetsmarknadsinstitutioner främjar sysselsättningen genom strukturomvandling i nyckelsektorer av ekonomin.
Resultat 2 (sektoriellt): Unga kvinnor och män som lever i fattigdom har tillgång till hållbara sysselsättningsmöjligheter i företag och ekonomiska enheter som övergår till högre produktivitet och koldioxidneutral produktion.
Resultat 3 (övergripande): Arbetsmarknadens parter och nyckelaktörer på nationell, provinsiell och lokal nivå har förmågan att bättre hantera viktiga begränsningar och flaskhalsar för att skapa anständig och produktiv sysselsättning genom systemisk och hållbar företagsutveckling och politiska insatser.
MozTrabalha 2 är ett femårigt projekt med en total budget om 144,5 miljoner SEK.

The overall objective of MozTrabalha 2 is to contribute to the creation of productive employment and decent working conditions for Mozambican women and men, particularly youth and those living in poverty. Three results will contribute to achieve the overall objective: - Outcome 1 (national): Supportive economic and sectoral policies and labor market institutions advance employment through structural transformation in key sectors of the economy.
- Outcome 2 (sectoral): Young women and men living in poverty – access sustainable employment opportunities in enterprises and economic units that transition to higher productivity and carbon-neutral production.
- Outcome 3 (cross-cutting): Tripartite constituents and key stakeholders at national, provincial and local levels are capacitated to better address key constraints and bottlenecks for decent and pro-poor employment creation through systemic and sustainable enterprise development and policy interventions.
MozTrabalha 2 is a five year project with a total budget of 144 500 000 million SEK. It will work on a systems level to address key bottle necks to job creation in key sectors.

The overall objective of MozTrabalha2 is to contribute to the creation of productive employment and decent working conditions for Mozambican women and men, particularly youth and those living in poverty.
Applying a systems approach as the guiding framework, the project will strive to achieve its objectives on the basis of interventions at the national and sectoral levels, as well as cross-cutting capacity development support to ILOs tripartite constituents and main stakeholders. Through this, the following three outcomes are foreseen:
Outcome 1 (national): Supportive economic and sectoral policies and labour market institutions advance employment through structural transformation in key sectors of the economy.
Outcome 2 (sectoral): Young women and men living in poverty access sustainable employment opportunities in enterprises and economic units that transition to higher productivity and carbon-neutral production.
Outcome 3 (cross-cutting): Tripartite constituents and key stakeholders at national, provincial and local levels are capacitated to better address key constraints and bottlenecks for decent and pro-poor employment creation through systemic and sustainable enterprise development and policy interventions.
The project is expected to achieve its objective through positively influencing the employment-intensity and productivity levels of economic growth in the country, as well as ensuring that resulting benefits go to the identified target groups, by influencing national and sectoral level growth dynamics, structural transformation trajectories, and just transitions to a low-carbon economy.
This overarching project-level impact goal will be achieved through a wide range of outcome and output level result goals, which in a systemic manner will contribute to its overall achievement. Concrete outcome and output level goals will be defined in subsequent steps through the projects dynamic and fluid design philosophy which is based on recurring learning cycles.

description.narrative:
Outcome 1 Employment policy reforms advance: An independent evaluation of the National Employment Policy (NEP) and its Action Plan (PAPE) provide several findings and recommendations related to relevance, impact and sustainability. These findings can inform the development of next NEP and PAPE. The development and introduction of the Pro-Employment Budgeting toolkit, supported by key ministries, is another process of interest, as is the ratification of ILO's Occupational Safety and Health (OSH) Convention and Protocol. The ratification of the OSH protocol also catalyzed work on new national OSH policy and specific regulation for the construction sector.
Outcome 2 In forestry and wood processing, systemic changes take shape: The project supports reforms with the aim of improving the working conditions and also broadening opportunities for workers and entrepreneurs. A new forest regulation has been supported, and ILO engage closely with the Mozambican Federation of Timber Operators. The pilot with the forestry company Portucel on "responsible digital wage payments" is another intervention of interest, with the aim to engage with the National Social Security Institute (INSS) and that seasonal forestry works would have access to social protection. The aim is to support INSS to advance towards the creation of a new social security regime for seasonal workers that will allow forestry and agricultural operators to contribute to INSS for informal seasonal workers and the latter to enjoy the INSS benefits. If successful, this pilot has significant scale-up potential, not only in the forestry sector, but also in the agricultural and other sectors in the Mozambican economy, contributing to a better business environment for enterprises, formalizing occasional and seasonal workers, and improve job quality by extending access to social protection to a part of the population that does not currently benefit from it. Furthermore, the service providers (subcontractors responsible for paying workers) claimed that the digitalization of payment enabled them to cut down their transaction costs by 20%, highlighting the potential for the adoption of the model by other forestry operators and in sectors beyond forestry. There is also a promising intervention in the biomass market with the potential of (formal) green jobs in the briquette and pellets production. ILO is as much as possible using the Market System Development approach.
Sustainable construction demonstrates viable pathways for greener, more affordable, and more job rich building models: The pilot project for climate smart housing has completed the construction of energy efficient homes. This intervention is assessed to have a number of interesting entry points, which include the use of greener building materials and improving the working conditions for constructions workers (more formal). A new rent-to-buy financial mechanism has been developed that could potentially open the housing market for a new market segment. In 2025 the first Mozambican market driven housing refinancing mechanism was operationalized, jointly designed with SDU Beira (a publicprivate municipal development enterprise), RVO (the Dutch Development Agency), Empowa (a Fintech provider) and the financial service provider GAPI, who is the ultimate implementer of the mechanism. The aim of the mechanism is to (a) increase access to climate smart housing for lower-and- middle income households, (b) offer housing developers access to finance to refinance and expand their stock of rent-to-buy houses, and (c) attract investors to scale up the mechanism with the final objective to (d) create more formal employment in the fast expanding affordable, climate smart and green housing sector. Following the successful release of its first loans to the developer Casa Real, the refinancing mechanism has been attracting strong attention from Government and development partners within and beyond Mozambique, as it offers an attractive alternative to dominant supply-driven approaches.
Outcome 3 Tripartite constituents strengthened their leadership in employment and decent work: Representatives from relevant institutions received training on pro-employment macroeconomic and sectoral policies, OSH, minimum wages, social dialogue and Just Transition. Sectoral dialogues in forestry and construction were also held, addressing specific opportunities and challenges within these industries.
